title: The letter as flesh, the spiritual sense as divinity
english: Just as in the last days the Word of God came forth from Mary clothed in flesh—one thing was seen, another was understood—so when the Word is brought forth through the prophets or the lawgiver, it is covered with the veil of the letter. The rites and sacrifices of Leviticus are as flesh in the letter; the spiritual sense is as divinity. Blessed are the eyes that see the Spirit hidden beneath the veil of the letter. Those who follow only the history are compelled to offer calves and lambs; the church uses the words of Susanna: it is better to fall into your hands than to sin against the Lord (Susanna 1:23). For those converted to the Lord the veil is taken away (2 Corinthians 3:16); where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom (2 Corinthians 3:17). Reveal my eyes, and I will consider the wonders of your law (Psalm 119:18).

orientation: Origen opens the homily by explaining how the Word of God comes veiled in the letter of Leviticus, just as Christ came veiled in flesh from Mary.

title: The call to secret things
english: The beginning of Leviticus: the Lord called Moses and spoke to him from the tabernacle. The call of God leads to secret things. He is not called to sacrifices in Egypt, but in the desert, in the tabernacle of testimony. Whoever is still in the Egypt of vices cannot offer spiritual sacrifices. Moses is called and receives the law of sacrifices — not so that the church may sacrifice Christ with bloody victims, but so that it may understand the reasonable burnt offering.

orientation: Origen is beginning his homily on Leviticus 1:1, explaining that God's call to Moses from the tabernacle is a call to spiritual understanding, not to literal sacrifice.

title: Laying on of hands and the blood of Christ
english: He will lay his hand upon the head of the victim, and it will be acceptable. The laying on of the hand signifies communion: the things that are offered become ours. Christ is the head; we are the members. To lay on the hand is to consent and to confess the sins that pass over into the victim. The blood is sprinkled at the altar: without the pouring out of blood there is no remission. Our high priest Christ offered himself once.

orientation: Origen is explaining the ritual of the burnt offering from Leviticus, interpreting each action as a figure of Christ and the Christian's participation in his sacrifice.

title: The flayed calf: the letter stripped away reveals the spiritual sense
english: They flay the burnt offering and divide it limb by limb; the sons of Aaron place the fire, the wood, and the divided pieces upon the altar. The calf is Christ; the skin of the letter stripped away opens the spiritual sense. To divide it limb by limb is to arrange the progress: to fit the teaching to beginners, to those advancing, and to the perfect. The wood of the altar is the passion of the flesh, even to the wood of the cross; the fire from above is the divinity. The entrails and the feet are washed with water: this is the sacrament of baptism.

title: The moral application of the calf offering
english: Now turn to the moral sense. You too have a calf—your proud flesh. If you wish to offer a gift to the Lord, lead it to the door of the tabernacle, which is the hearing of the divine books. Let your gift be male; lay your hand on it and cut its throat before the Lord—that is, the bridle of self-control: I bruise my body (1 Corinthians 9:27). Let the sons of Aaron in you—mind and sense—offer the blood. Offer a living victim, holy, pleasing to God (Romans 12:1). Here ends Homily I. Amen.
